children: OTTAWA--Canada posted a third-quarter current-account surplus, marking the first time in about four years the country has recorded two consecutive quarterly surpluses, though it was smaller than expected.

Canada's current account, the broadest indicator of its trading and investing relationship with other nations, recorded a seasonally adjusted surplus of 4.48 billion Canadian dollars ($3.14 billion) in the third quarter, Statistics Canada said Friday. That fell short of expectations for a C$9.4 billion surplus, according to Bank of Nova Scotia.
The data agency revised the previous quarter's surplus to C$6.10 billion, from an earlier estimate of C$8.84 billion.
